\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ریڈیو} (reḍiyo)}{ریڈیو (reḍiyo)}]{\ur{ریڈیو} (reḍiyo) — a radio}

\label{lesson:UR-C300-rediyo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for morale, then the Urdu for a donation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ریڈیو}}
\textbf{\ur{ریڈیو}} — \emph{reḍiyo} — \textquotedblleft{}a radio\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ریڈیو} \ur{پر} \ur{گاؤں} \ur{کی} \ur{خبر} \ur{آئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{reḍiyo par gāoṅ kī khabar āī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The news about the village came on the radio.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ریڈیو}} (\emph{reḍiyo}) is borrowed from English \emph{radio}. News comes \textbf{\ur{ریڈیو} \ur{پر}}, on the radio.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reḍiyo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reḍiyo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reḍiyo par gāoṅ kī khabar āī.} — The news about the village came on the radio.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for morale, then the Urdu for a donation, then say \emph{reḍiyo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ریڈیو} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A radio\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نشر} \ur{کرنا} (nashr karnā)}{نشر کرنا (nashr karnā)}]{\ur{نشر} \ur{کرنا} (nashr karnā) — to broadcast}

\label{lesson:UR-C300-nashr-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a donation, then the Urdu for a radio.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نشر} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{نشر} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{nashr karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to broadcast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ریڈیو} \ur{نے} \ur{خبر} \ur{نشر} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{reḍiyo ne khabar nashr kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The radio broadcast the news.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{اعلان} \ur{نشر} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne elān nashr kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نشر} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{nashr karnā}) is built from \emph{nashr}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{nashr}, \textquotedblleft{}a spreading out\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}: to spread news over the air. What is broadcast agrees: \textbf{\ur{خبر} \ur{نشر} \ur{کی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nashr karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nashr karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reḍiyo ne khabar nashr kī.} — The radio broadcast the news.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a donation, then the Urdu for a radio, then say \emph{nashr karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{نشر} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To broadcast\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سرخی} (surkhī)}{سرخی (surkhī)}]{\ur{سرخی} (surkhī) — a headline}

\label{lesson:UR-C300-surkhi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a radio, then the Urdu for to broadcast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سرخی}}
\textbf{\ur{سرخی}} — \emph{surkhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a headline\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اخبار} \ur{میں} \ur{بڑی} \ur{سرخی} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{akhbār meṅ baṛī surkhī thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a big headline in the paper.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سرخی}} (\emph{surkhī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{surkhī}, \textquotedblleft{}redness\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{surkh}, \textquotedblleft{}red\textquotedblright{}; headlines are thought to take the name from the red ink they were once printed in.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{surkhī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akhbār meṅ baṛī surkhī thī.} — There was a big headline in the paper.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a radio, then the Urdu for to broadcast, then say \emph{surkhī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اطلاع} (ittilā)}{اطلاع (ittilā)}]{\ur{اطلاع} (ittilā) — an official notice; word sent}

\label{lesson:UR-C300-ittila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to broadcast, then the Urdu for a headline.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اطلاع}}
\textbf{\ur{اطلاع}} — \emph{ittilā} — \textquotedblleft{}an official notice; word sent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پولیس} \ur{کو} \ur{اطلاع} \ur{ملی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīs ko ittilā milī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police were informed.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اطلاع}} (\emph{ittilā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iṭṭilāʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}a coming to know\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{اطلاع} \ur{ملی}} says word reached someone; \textbf{\ur{اطلاع} \ur{دینا}} is to inform.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ittilā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ittilā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polīs ko ittilā milī.} — The police were informed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to broadcast, then the Urdu for a headline, then say \emph{ittilā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سنسنی} (sansanī)}{سنسنی (sansanī)}]{\ur{سنسنی} (sansanī) — a sensation; excitement}

\label{lesson:UR-C300-sansani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a headline, then the Urdu for an official notice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سنسنی}}
\textbf{\ur{سنسنی}} — \emph{sansanī} — \textquotedblleft{}a sensation; excitement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{خبر} \ur{سے} \ur{شہر} \ur{میں} \ur{سنسنی} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is khabar se shahr meṅ sansanī thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The news caused a sensation in the city.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سنسنی}} (\emph{sansanī}) belongs with \emph{sansanānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to whizz, to be excited\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{svaná}, \textquotedblleft{}a noise\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13901): the hum that runs through a crowd.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sansanī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sansanī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is khabar se shahr meṅ sansanī thī.} — The news caused a sensation in the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a headline, then the Urdu for an official notice, then say \emph{sansanī} again
\end{itemize}
